# Sparkus

> TypeScript backend framework: decorators and dependency injection, compiled at startup, served by Bun.serve (under Bun) or node:http (under Node). Zero runtime dependencies. Every error has a stable code (SPKxxxx).

Install `sparkus`; tests use `@sparkus/testing`; the `sparkus` command comes from `@sparkus/cli`.

## Complete example

```ts
import { Controller, Get, Post, HttpError, createApp, inject, t, type Ctx } from "sparkus";

class UserService {
    find(id: number) { return id === 1 ? { id, name: "Ada" } : undefined; }
}

const GetUser = { params: t.object({ id: t.integer({ min: 1 }) }) };
const CreateUser = { body: t.object({ name: t.string({ min: 1 }) }), status: 201 };

@Controller("/users")
export class UserController {
    private readonly users = inject(UserService);

    @Get("/:id", GetUser)
    get(ctx: Ctx<typeof GetUser>) {               // ctx.params.id: number
        const user = this.users.find(ctx.params.id);
        if (!user) throw HttpError.notFound(`User ${ctx.params.id} not found.`, { code: "USER_NOT_FOUND" });
        return user;                               // objects are sent as JSON
    }

    @Post("", CreateUser)
    create(ctx: Ctx<typeof CreateUser>) {          // ctx.body: { name: string }, already validated
        return { id: 2, name: ctx.body.name };
    }
}

export default createApp({ controllers: [UserController] });   // src/app.ts
// src/main.ts: await app.listen();   (port: PORT env or 3000)
```

## Routes

- `@Controller(prefix)` on a class; it must be listed in `createApp({ controllers })`.
- `@Get`, `@Post`, `@Put`, `@Patch`, `@Delete`, `@Head`, `@Options` on public instance methods: `(path, options?)`.
- Paths: static segments and `:name` parameters. Case-sensitive; a trailing slash is a different path; static segments win over parameters. HEAD falls back to GET. Unknown path: 404 (SPK2001). Known path, other method: 405 with `Allow` (SPK2002).
- Options: `{ params?, query?, body?, response?, status?, bodyLimit?, timeout? }`. `response` types what the handler returns (checked at compile time), keeps only its fields in the response, and documents it in OpenAPI. Declare them as a `const` and type the handler with `Ctx<typeof Options>`. A handler that does not match (wrong return type, wrong `Ctx`) is reported by TypeScript on the decorator (TS1241); the last lines of the error name the mismatch.

## Schemas (`t`)

`t.string({ min, max })`, `t.integer({ min, max })`, `t.number({ min, max })`, `t.boolean()`, `t.enum(["draft", "published"])` (a union of strings), `t.object({ ... })`, `t.array(item, { min, max })`, `t.optional(schema)` (may be absent: `T | undefined`), `t.nullable(schema)` (may be `null`: `T | null`; both combine). Not allowed in `params`/`query` (SPK1017). Scalars and enums take a `default`: `t.integer({ min: 1, default: 1 })`, `t.enum(["asc", "desc"], { default: "asc" })`: an absent body field or query parameter gets it, so the field is always present (its type is not optional). Not on path parameters (SPK1017); a default that fails its own schema is SPK1017.

- `body`: any schema. JSON only (`content-type: application/json`, else 415 SPK2005), 1 MiB by default (413 SPK2006). Invalid: 400 SPK2004 with `issues: [{ path: "$.age", message }]`. Fields the schema does not list are dropped, at every depth: `ctx.body` holds exactly its type, and an absent optional field is absent (not `undefined`), so `{ ...entity, ...ctx.body }` is safe.
- `response`: fields the schema does not list are dropped before interceptors run and before sending (a `passwordHash` on an entity never leaks). Return your entities as they are. A value whose shape does not match (an object or array where the schema says otherwise) answers 500 SPK5001 naming the route and the path.
- `params`: flat `t.object` naming exactly the path's parameters, all required. Values converted (integer, number, boolean "true"/"false"/"1"/"0").
- `query`: flat `t.object`, fields usually `t.optional(...)`; unknown keys dropped. Invalid params/query: 400 SPK2004, `issues[0].path` is `params.id` or `query.page`.
- Without a schema: `ctx.params` / `ctx.query` are strings.
- Standard Schema: any `body`, `params`, `query` or `response` may be a Zod, Valibot or ArkType schema (anything implementing https://standardschema.dev) instead of a `t` schema. Types are inferred the same way (`Ctx<typeof Route>`). Its `validate()` runs as is (async checks are awaited); `ctx.body` / `ctx.params` / `ctx.query` get the library's output, the response sends the schema's output. Unknown fields are dropped if the library drops them (Zod and Valibot objects do; ArkType needs `"+": "delete"`). Params and query arrive as strings: use the library's coercion (`z.coerce.number()`). Errors keep Sparkus' shape (400 SPK2004, first issue, library's message; 500 SPK5001 for the response). OpenAPI uses the library's JSON Schema when it provides one (Zod 4 does). `t` schemas are faster (compiled): prefer them; use a library schema when you already have one.

## Ctx (handlers, guards, interceptors)

`method`, `path`, `params`, `query`, `body`, `header(name)`, `status` (settable), `setHeader(name, value)`, `state` (per-request object shared with guards and interceptors), `requestId` (the client's `x-request-id` when safe, else a UUID), `log` (logger whose lines carry the request id), `signal` (aborted when the client disconnects or the request times out: pass it to `fetch` and database calls). Type `state` with the second parameter: `ctx: Ctx<typeof CreatePost, { user: User }>` (not checked at runtime: the guard that sets it must run on that route).

Return value: object/array/number/null → JSON; string → text/plain; `Uint8Array` → octet-stream; `undefined` → 204 (or the route status if not 200); a `Response` is sent as is. Handlers may be async.

## Dependency injection

- Services are plain classes without constructor parameters (`constructor(private users: UserService)` is SPK1009). Get one with `private readonly x = inject(XService)` in a field initializer or constructor, never in a method (SPK1001). Singletons, created at startup.
- Values: `export const DB_URL = token<string>("DB_URL")`, then `createApp({ providers: [{ provide: DB_URL, useValue: "..." }] })`. Providers: `useValue`, `useClass`, `useFactory` (may call `inject`).
- Lifecycle: `onInit()` (dependencies first, may be async, awaited before listening) and `onShutdown()` (reverse order).
- `app.get(Token)` resolves a singleton.

## Configuration

```ts
// src/config.ts
export const AppConfig = config({
    DATABASE_URL: t.string({ min: 1 }),
    PORT: t.integer({ min: 1, default: 3000 }),
    MODE: t.enum(["live", "sandbox"], { default: "sandbox" }),
    ALLOWED_ORIGINS: t.optional(t.array(t.string())),   // comma-separated
});
// in a service: private readonly config = inject(AppConfig);   this.config.PORT is a number
```

Keys are environment variable names. Fields: `t.string`, `t.integer`, `t.number`, `t.boolean` ("true"/"false"/"1"/"0"), `t.enum`, `t.array` of those; `t.optional` or `default` for optional variables; an empty variable is unset. Read from `process.env` at startup (Bun loads `.env` itself; under Node use `node --env-file=.env`). Missing or invalid variables stop the app with SPK1018, listing all of them (values are never printed); a `default` inside `t.optional()` is refused. In tests: `overrides: [AppConfig.override({ PAGE_SIZE: 5 })]` (typed, checked, defaults and environment kept for the rest). `listen()` reads `PORT` itself (default 3000, invalid: SPK1018); declare it in `config()` too and pass `listen({ port })` to keep one source.

## Logging

`private readonly log = inject(Logger).child("users")`, then `this.log.info("User created", { userId })`, `this.log.error("Payment failed", error)` (the second argument is an object of fields, or anything else, such as a `catch` variable, logged as `err`). In handlers prefer `ctx.log` (adds `reqId`). With `logger: { requestContext: true }`, every logger adds the `reqId` (and the server span's `trace_id`, `span_id`) of the request being handled, services included, across awaits (AsyncLocalStorage: about 4 % of throughput under Node, under 1 % under Bun). Levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal. One JSON object per line (`{"level":"info","time":1760000000000,"module":"users","msg":"...","userId":1}`), readable lines in a terminal.

`createApp({ logger: { level, modules: { db: "debug" }, format: "json" | "pretty", requests: true, requestContext: true, write } })`; `logger: false` for none. `LOG_LEVEL=info,db=debug` sets the levels, only when the code gives no `level` (then `modules` merge over it). Request lines use the module "http" (`modules: { http: "warn" }` silences them), Sparkus' own lines "sparkus". Default level: info (warn under NODE_ENV=test). `requests: true` logs one line per request (`msg: "GET /users/1 200"`, `method`, `path`, `route`, `status`, `ms`, `reqId`).

## Production options

```ts
createApp({
    controllers,
    logger: { requests: true, requestContext: true },   // request lines; reqId in every line logged during a request
    cors: { origin: ["https://app.example.com"], credentials: true },   // or cors: true for any origin
    securityHeaders: true,            // CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-options...; { "strict-transport-security": false } drops one
    requestId: true,                  // echo x-request-id in every response
    health: true,                     // GET /health (liveness), GET /ready (runs every HealthCheck service)
    requestTimeout: 30_000,           // 503 SPK2008 and ctx.signal aborted after 30 s (async work only); route option `timeout` overrides
    telemetry: { tracer: trace.getTracer("api"), meter: metrics.getMeter("api") },   // @opentelemetry/api
});
await app.listen({ shutdownDelay: 5_000, idleTimeout: 65_000 });
```

- Everything is off by default and costs nothing when off. CORS, security and request id headers are on every response, errors and 404 included; a header the handler sets wins. A CORS preflight (OPTIONS with `access-control-request-method`) on a path with routes answers 204 with that path's methods. Origins are exact (`https://app.example.com`, no trailing slash: SPK1019), RegExps, or a function `(origin) => boolean` (a throw refuses the origin); `origin: "*"` refuses `credentials`. A handler that sets `vary` replaces the `vary: origin` CORS adds: include `origin` in it.
- Readiness: a service with `checkHealth()` (implements `HealthCheck`) is called by `/ready`; throwing or returning `false` gives 503 SPK2009 naming it. From the shutdown signal on (and in `app.close()`), `/ready` answers 503; on a signal, `shutdownDelay` keeps serving that long first, so load balancers stop sending traffic. Checks are the services the container built (injected somewhere), found on the first probe; `useValue` providers are not checked. Probes skip guards and are left out of OpenAPI.
- Telemetry: a server span per request named `GET /users/:id` with the HTTP semantic convention attributes, errors recorded on 5xx, and the `http.server.request.duration` histogram (seconds). `extract: (ctx) => ...` gives the parent context (traceparent), `activate: (span, run) => context.with(trace.setSpan(context.active(), span), run)` makes your spans its children.

## Guards and interceptors

```ts
const isAdmin = (ctx: Ctx) => ctx.header("authorization") === "Bearer admin";   // true lets the request through
class AuthGuard implements Guard { users = inject(UserService); canActivate(ctx: Ctx) { ...; return true; } }
const timing: InterceptorFn = async (ctx, next) => { const r = await next(); ctx.setHeader("x-t", "1"); return r; };
```

`@UseGuards(...)` / `@UseInterceptors(...)` on a controller or a method; `createApp({ guards, interceptors })` for all routes. Order: params/query conversion, guards (app, controller, route), interceptors (app outermost), body, validation, handler. A guard returning anything but `true` gives 403 (SPK2007); throw an `HttpError` for another status.

## Errors

- `throw new HttpError(status, detail?, { code?, extensions?, headers? })`, or `HttpError.badRequest / unauthorized / forbidden / notFound / conflict / unprocessable / tooManyRequests(detail, options)`. Sent as `application/problem+json`: `{ type, title, status, detail, code, ...extensions }`.
- Any other thrown error: logged, 500 SPK5000; its message is sent only when `exposeErrors` is on (default in development and test). Stacks are never sent.
- `createApp({ onError: (error, ctx) => error instanceof MyError ? HttpError.conflict(error.message) : undefined })` maps your errors.
- Startup errors (SPK1xxx) stop `init()` / `listen()`: the message names the culprit and the fix. Reference: docs/errors.md.

## App

`createApp({ controllers, providers?, guards?, interceptors?, onError?, exposeErrors?, bodyLimit?, requestTimeout?, logger?, cors?, securityHeaders?, requestId?, health?, telemetry?, engine? })`

- `await app.listen({ port?, hostname?, signals?, shutdownTimeout?, shutdownDelay?, idleTimeout? })` → `{ engine, port, url }`. SIGINT/SIGTERM: readiness fails, wait `shutdownDelay`, stop accepting, finish in-flight requests (up to `shutdownTimeout`), `onShutdown`, exit.
- `await app.init()` wires everything without listening. `app.routes` lists the routes. `app.fetch(request)` is a web-standard handler.
- `app.openapi({ title, version })` returns the OpenAPI 3.1 document built from the route schemas (after `init()`).
- `await app.close()` shuts down.
- `engine`: `"auto"` (default), `"bun"`, `"node"`.

## Testing

```ts
import { createTestApp } from "@sparkus/testing";
const app = await createTestApp({ controllers, providers, overrides: [{ provide: UserService, useValue: fake }] });
const res = await app.inject({ method: "POST", url: "/users", body: { name: "Ada" } });
res.status; res.json(); res.headers; res.text;
```

In memory, full pipeline, no port. `createTestApp` takes the same options as `createApp`: export them from `src/app.ts` (`export const options: AppOptions = {...}; export default createApp(options)`) and test the same app: `createTestApp({ ...options, overrides })`. A new app per test keeps singletons from leaking state between tests. `app.get(Token)` returns a singleton (a fake to inspect). `app.fetch(request)` is the web-standard handler, for a generated client: `createClient({ baseUrl: "http://test", fetch: (request) => app.fetch(request) })`.

## CLI

- `sparkus init <dir>`: new project with AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills, check hook.
- `sparkus check [entry] --json`: wire the app without listening; `{ ok, error: { code, message } }`. `warnings` lists controllers in `*.controller.ts` files that serve no route (missing from `controllers`).
- `sparkus routes [entry] --json`: list routes.
- `sparkus openapi [entry]`: print the OpenAPI 3.1 document.
- `sparkus client [entry] --out src/client.ts`: generate a typed client (one file, no dependency): `const api = createClient({ baseUrl })`, then `await api.user.get({ params: { id: 42 } })` (group = controller name without `Controller`, method = handler name; input `{ params, query, body }`, second argument `{ headers, signal }`). Return types come from `response` schemas (`unknown` without one). Non-2xx responses throw `ApiError` (`status`, `code`, `problem`). In tests, pass `fetch: (request) => app.fetch(request)`. Run it again after changing a route.
- `sparkus dev [entry]`: run and restart on changes under src/.

The entry exports the app (`export default app`), `src/app.ts` by default.
